candidate.title: TruSeq Targeted RNA Expression
candidate.scope: The single, unbranched TruSeq Targeted RNA Expression library-preparation schematic in the assigned Illumina poster panel: total RNA to cDNA, custom ULSO/DLSO targeting, extension–ligation, and indexed amplification ending with a DNA product ready for cluster generation. No kit revision or protocol version is stated. The drawing supports this product-preparation architecture rather than a complete experimental implementation.

operations.label: Hybridization
operations.description: Positions the added ULSO and DLSO on flanking regions of the same cDNA template, leaving the target interval between their inner ends. Free oligonucleotides become a template-associated pair.
operations.mechanism: Hybridization to the cDNA, as labeled and drawn; the DLSO 5′P is preserved in the hybridized complex.
operations.information_effect: Associates both targeting oligonucleotides with the cDNA interval selected for the subsequent extension–ligation product. The cartoon does not measure binding specificity.

evidence.locator: Hybridization row: ULSO and 5′P-bearing DLSO aligned on the cDNA on opposite sides of the target interval

operations.label: Extension-Ligation
operations.description: Converts the two separated template-bound oligonucleotides into one continuous upper DNA strand spanning the target interval, while the cDNA template remains underneath.
operations.mechanism: Template-directed extension across the gap and ligation to the DLSO are inferred from the labeled step and the separate-to-continuous strand change. The DLSO junction-facing 5′P is explicitly depicted; particular enzymes are not identified.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the target association into a continuous joined DNA construct containing the flanking oligonucleotide segments and intervening target-templated segment.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Denatures the extension–ligation material, shown as separated DNA strands, and amplifies with the illustrated P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 primers to produce the paired-strand, indexed target library. These are a single combined operation at the figure’s resolution.
operations.mechanism: Denaturation and primer-mediated amplification are explicitly labeled; the primer tails become terminal regions of the final library.
operations.information_effect: Carries the target-associated DNA into an amplified construct with two indexes and P5/P7 ends, providing the depicted interface to cluster generation. Target-region sequence can associate library molecules with the designed RNA target; the diagram does not establish a calibration from library counts to original transcript numbers.

checks.rationale: All eight states, five local operations and twelve material flows were checked against the complete image, including their interfaces and preparation histories. Every depicted transformation is represented: RNA-to-cDNA conversion, custom-primer addition, hybridization, extension-ligation and combined denaturation/amplification leading to an indexed cluster-ready product. RNA is the starting biological target material; the final carrier is amplified target-associated DNA derived through the joined oligonucleotide product. The 5′P, template association, target gap, joined-strand change, dual indexes and P5/P7 interface are retained. The two multi-input operations are additions to one route, not independently processed branches; no branch, compartment or depicted alternative is omitted. The card is catalogue evidence and supplies no references or required primary-paper association. Empty paper_matches is appropriate, and no unavailable full text, historical claim or paper-based correction is asserted. No consequential unsupported assertion, source conflict or missing architecture-changing fact was found within this declared schematic scope.
